tax_exemption: Separate PBO application to SARS (IT321/IT361 + NPO certificate) under s.30 Income Tax Act; grants income tax exemption + 18A donor deduction; no statutory deadline, typically weeks to months.
Separate ANBI decision (beschikking) from Belastingdienst: public-benefit purpose + 90%-of-activity rule; grants CIT exemption + 30% donor deduction; usually 2-4 weeks, no statutory deadline.
No separate tax registration: ASBL with charitable purpose is income-tax-exempt on non-profit activity; 90% donor tax reduction requires listing on the FPS Economy public-utility list (BCE/KBO).

Automatic: income of non-profit associations/foundations is exempt from CIT without a separate tax procedure (checked at filing). Donations get 25% deduction, 50% for extra gifts, capped at 1% of taxable income.

Automatic: association loi 1901 with general-interest purpose is income-tax-exempt with no separate procedure (CGI art. 208). Donors get 66% tax reduction, capped at 20% of taxable income. No VAT exemption.

Separate Freistellungsbescheid from the Finanzamt: must meet the charitable catalogue (AO ss.52-68, non-profit, member base, public benefit). Grants income tax exemption + 30% donor deduction; usually weeks to 3 months.

Separate application to the Finanzamt for s.34 EStG privileged taxation (zugunftsbesteuerung, public-benefit purpose). Grants income tax exemption + donor deduction (20% individuals/25% companies); weeks to months.

Generally automatic: cantonal tax authority exempts foundations/associations whose articles serve common benefit (gemeinnuetzig) at filing - no separate procedure. Donations deductible (c. CHF 25-35k).
Automatic: foundations/associations with non-profit, common-benefit articles are income-tax-exempt under s.15 EStG without any separate tax procedure. Donations are not deductible; no VAT exemption.

No personal income tax on residents, so foundations/associations face no domestic income tax; public-utility status (sovereign decree) is a civil, not tax, step. Donors deduct in home states (e.g. France 66-75%).
Automatic: foundations and associations with charitable purpose are exempt from IRPOS (corporate income tax) by law, no separate tax application. No general donor deduction; no VAT.

Automatic: non-profit foundations/associations with charitable purpose are exempt from personal income tax (Llei 5/2014 s.33) with no separate procedure; donor deduction limited (20%, capped at 1% of income).

Separate: fundacja/stowarzyszenie registers as OPP (public benefit) at the Ministry of the Interior to access 1% personal tax donation + gift deduction; income tax applies to business activity. No VAT exemption.
Separate: spolek applies for ZU (general-benefit) status at the Ministry of Interior register. Grants income tax exemption on non-business income + 4% personal tax donation. No VAT exemption.
Separate: VPO (public-benefit) status by Ministry of Interior decision under Act 65/2018. Grants income tax exemption + 1% personal tax donation + gift deduction. No VAT exemption.

Separate NAV procedure: apply for income tax exemption (adozo-kiveteles status) + annual 1% registration (form 25EGYREG, capped at 2%). Corporate donations deductible (1.5% total). Decision typically within 30 days.

Automatic: associations/foundations are income-tax-exempt on non-business activity (ZDavO s.9) with no separate tax procedure. 'Javno koristno' is a civil-law status; donors get 25% deduction (max EUR 200).
Separate: 'javno korisna' (public-benefit) decision by the Ministry of Interior. Grants income tax exemption + 2% personal / 1% corporate tax donation + 40% gift deduction. No published deadline.

Application to the tax administration (FBiH/Trezor): non-profit entities with charitable purpose are exempt from PIT under the BiH PIT Law if conditions met; gifts partially deductible; no published deadline.

Largely automatic: udruzenje gracana is income-tax-exempt on non-profit income (Income Tax Law s.18) where purpose serves public interest; access to 1% personal tax and 2% corporate donations. No statutory deadline.
